fb: One of four rivers that branch from the river watering Eden, said to wind around the land of Havilah, where there is gold, bdellium and onyx. Nobody has ever pinned it on a map.

H6310.d: the mouth (as the means of blowing), whether literal or figurative (particularly speech); specifically edge, portion or side; adverbially (with preposition) according to

H6316.d: Put, a son of Ham, also the name of his descendants or their region, and of a Persian tribe
fb: A son of Ham in the table of nations. The prophets tie his descendants to northern Africa, likely ancient Libya, and keep listing them among the hired soldiers in other people's armies.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Genesis and 1 Chronicles name him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

H6327.d: to dash in pieces, literally or figuratively (especially to disperse)

fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
In his days the earth was divided, Genesis says. That is usually taken to mean the scattering at Babel. He came down from Shem.

H6381.d: properly, perhaps to separate, i.e. distinguish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to be (causatively, make) great, difficult, wonderful

H6311.d: this place (French ici), i.e. here or hence

fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
He commanded Abimelech's army, and was there when Abimelech made peace with Abraham, and again a generation later with Isaac.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Nahor, Abraham's brother, had eight sons by Milcah, and Pildash was one.

H6307.d: Paddan or Paddan-Aram, a region of Syria
fb: Short for Paddan-aram, the country around Haran in upper Mesopotamia where Abraham's brother Nahor settled. Rebekah came from there. Jacob ran there years later to get away from Esau.

H6343.d: a (sudden) alarm (properly, the object feared, by implication, the feeling)

fb: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
An Edomite chief in Genesis 36:41 and 1 Chronicles 1:52, whom many scholars take to be the same name as Punon.
Egyptian living at the time of the Patriarchs
An Egyptian official. He bought Joseph as a slave and soon had him running the whole household. When Potiphar's wife accused Joseph falsely, Potiphar had him put in prison.
Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
Priest of On. His daughter Asenath married Joseph after Pharaoh raised Joseph up, so Ephraim and Manasseh were his grandsons.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Reuben's son. His descendants, the Palluites, were one of the clans counted in the wilderness.

H6312.d: Puah or Puvvah, the name of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Issachar's son, usually spelled Puvah, in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.
Judges names him once, and he is a man from the years before the monarchy.

H6339.d: to solidify (as if by refining); also to spring (as if separating the limbs)

fb: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Pharaoh ordered her and Shiphrah, two Hebrew midwives, to kill the Israelite baby boys at birth. They feared God more than Pharaoh, let the boys live, and God rewarded them for it.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
His daughter married Eleazar, Aaron's son, and their son was Phinehas. Putiel himself is a name and nothing more.

H6372.d: Pinechas, the name of three Israelites
fb: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

Aaron's grandson, Eleazar's son. When Israel was being struck by a plague for idolatry and sexual sin with Moabite women, Phinehas drove a spear through an Israelite man and a Midianite woman together, and the plague stopped.
Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
One of Eli's corrupt sons, killed in battle on the same day the Philistines captured the Ark of the Covenant.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Phinehas. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Ezra.

H6368.d: a powder (as easily puffed away), i.e. ashes or dust

H6363.d: a fissure, i.e. (concretely) firstling (as opening the matrix)

fb: Israel doubled back from Etham and camped here beside the sea, and Pharaoh's army came up behind them. It was here that Moses stretched out his hand over the water.

H6341.d: a (metallic) sheet (as pounded thin); also a spring net (as spread out like a lamina)

H6356.d: a hole (by mildew in a garment)

fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Father of the man who led Manasseh in the wilderness census.

H6302.d: as abstractly (in plural masculine) a ransom

H6384.d: a Palluite (collectively) or descendants of Pallu
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Pallu's descendants, a clan of Reuben counted in the wilderness census, and listed once.

H6324.d: a Punite (collectively) or descendants of an unknown Pun
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
The clan of Puvah, Issachar's son, counted in the census of Numbers 26.

H6325.d: Punon, a place in the Desert
fb: Israel camped here between Zalmonah and Oboth, and it is identified with Phaeno, where early Christian writers placed Roman copper mines.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Son of Ammihud, and the leader from Naphtali whom Moses picked to help share out Canaan among the tribes. His name means "God has redeemed."

H6342.d: to be startled (by a sudden alarm); hence, to fear in general

H6348.d: to bubble up or froth (as boiling water), i.e. (figuratively) to be unimportant

H6378.d: a flask (from which a liquid may flow)

H6362.d: to cleave or burst through, i.e. (causatively) to emit, whether literal or figurative (gape)

H6354.d: a pit, especially for catching animals

H6346.d: a prefect (of a city or small district)

H6398.d: to slice, i.e. break open or pierce

H6322.d: Pul, the name of an Assyrian king and of an Ethiopian tribe
fb: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Another Old Testament name for the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser the Third, the one Menahem of Israel paid off to keep his own throne.
Named once, in Isaiah, and nowhere else.

H6305.d: Pedajah, the name of six Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
In the royal line after the exile, named in 1 Chronicles 3:18-19 in the same breath as Zerubbabel.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 7 men called Pedaiah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
2 Kings names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 7 men called Pedaiah. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return, and Nehemiah is the only book that names him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return. Nehemiah names him once.

H6336.d: a Puthite (collectively) or descendants of an unknown Puth

fb: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
In the line of King Saul that runs through Jonathan, Pithon is a son of Micah and a grandson of Mephibosheth.

H6397.d: a Pelonite or inhabitant of an unknown Palon
fb: Warriors, perhaps from Pelon or Palet
Two of David's mighty men, Helez and Ahijah, carry this label. Where it points is unclear, and it may just be another spelling of Paltite.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A big family among the returning exiles, big enough that Ezra and Nehemiah both list it house by house.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Pahathmoab. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
His family were Nethinim, temple servants who came back from Babylon with Zerubbabel, and nothing further is recorded about him.

H6380.d: Pokereth-Tsebajim, one of the 'servants of Solomon'

H6332.d: a lot (as by means of a broken piece)
fb: It means a lot, the thing Haman cast to pick a date for killing the Jews. Purim takes its name from it, which reads like a joke at his expense.

H6340.d: to scatter, whether in enmity or bounty

fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Haman had ten sons. Poratha was one, killed by the Jews of Susa when they defended themselves against the slaughter Haman had planned, and Purim remembers it.

H6388.d: a rill (i.e. small channel of water, as in irrigation)

H6344.d: a testicle (as a cause of shame akin to fear)

H6315.d: to puff, i.e. blow with the breath or air; hence, to fan (as a breeze), to utter, to kindle (a fire), to scoff

H6323.d: meaning to turn, i.e. be perplexed

H6329.d: to issue, i.e. furnish; causatively, to secure; figuratively, to succeed

H6352.d: a coal, whether charred or live

fb: Ezekiel says its young men will fall by the sword. The Greeks called it Bubastis, a city in the eastern Nile Delta and the center of worship for the cat goddess Bastet.

H6361.d: a gown (as if hammered out wide)

H6393.d: a cleaver, i.e. iron armature (of a chariot)
